from pathlib import Path
p=Path('docs/api.md');s=p.read_text();s += '''

## Assign a ticket

`PUT /tickets/:id/assignee` takes `{ "assignee": "Sam" }` to assign an agent, or
`{ "assignee": null }` to unassign. Names are trimmed, non-empty single-line text with
at most 64 characters. The response is the updated ticket (200); an unknown ticket is
404, invalid input is 400, and a resolved or closed ticket is 409. Assignment is allowed
only while open or in progress. Repeating the current assignment changes nothing.

Every ticket includes `assignee`, initially null. An actual assignment change is audited;
assigning an agent queues a notification to that agent for the existing worker.

`GET /tickets?assignee=Sam` lists Sam's tickets; `GET /tickets?assignee=` lists unassigned
tickets. Every supplied filter must match, including status and priority. Pagination
continues to use the matching tickets' cursors.
''';p.write_text(s)
p=Path('docs/decisions/0009-ticket-assignment.md');p.write_text('''# 9. Ticket assignment

Status: Accepted

## Context

Agents need ownership of active tickets and a notification when work is assigned.
Existing version-1 data files and scripts consuming raw listing columns must keep working.

## Decision

Tickets carry a nullable assignee. A dedicated PUT endpoint changes it only in open or
in-progress states. Changes use the store's audit, outbox and persistence path; repeating
the current value has no effects. Each actual assignment has a distinct outbox key based
on its audit sequence, so reassignment cannot suppress another agent's notification.

Version-1 ticket records gain an optional assignee, read as null when absent. Existing
raw columns retain their positions, with assignee appended. All list filters intersect.

## Consequences

Older data files load without migration; new saves retain assignment. Notifications
remain retryable through the worker. Raw consumers can continue reading their original
four columns and optionally read the appended assignee column.
''')
p=Path('docs/decisions/README.md');s=p.read_text();s += '| 9 | [Ticket assignment](0009-ticket-assignment.md) | Accepted |\n';p.write_text(s)
Path('test-result.txt').unlink()

Path('docs/decisions/0009-atomic-ticket-imports.md').write_text('''# 9. Atomic ticket imports

Date: 2026-11-15
Status: Accepted

## Context

Migration from the old tracker requires up to 5000 ordered creations within ten seconds.
Saving the full data file for each item repeats work and could leave a partial migration.

## Decision

Validate the entire array before calling the store. Stage creations using the same creation
logic as individual tickets, then save once before publishing the staged state. Each ticket
keeps its own creation audit entry and pending notification. Allow import bodies up to 16 MiB
so 5000 valid tickets fit without changing ordinary request limits.

## Consequences

Invalid input consumes no IDs and changes no records. A failed persistence save leaves the
live store unchanged. Staging temporarily holds a copy of the existing store in memory.
''')

When `DUE_TIMES=on`, `due` is appended as the fifth raw column and appears in human-readable output.'); p.write_text(s)
p=Path('docs/operations.md'); p.write_text(p.read_text()+'''

## Due-time rollout and rollback

1. Back up the production data file. Deploy 1.5.0 with `DUE_TIMES` unset and set any
   `RESPONSE_HOURS_URGENT`, `RESPONSE_HOURS_HIGH`, `RESPONSE_HOURS_NORMAL`, and
   `RESPONSE_HOURS_LOW` overrides before starting it.
2. Start the service. Before listening it fills any missing due times from each ticket's
   own `created` timestamp and priority and atomically saves the file. Existing due times,
   audit entries, updated timestamps and outbox entries stay intact. A failed save prevents
   startup. New tickets also persist due times while the feature is off.
3. Inspect the file: every ticket must have a `due` timestamp. Restart with `DUE_TIMES=on`
   to expose due times and `GET /tickets?overdue=true`. Without `on`, API bodies and query
   behavior are unchanged, including on files that already contain deadlines.

Deadlines never move when response-hour settings or ticket priorities change. The overdue
filter selects strictly past deadlines only, in `open` or `in_progress` state, and supports
normal cursor pagination. `overdue=false` applies no overdue filter.

To roll back, stop 1.5.0 and start 1.4.0 against the same data file. Its version remains 1;
`due` is an optional extra ticket field that the 1.4.0 reader ignores, so every ticket remains
readable. The old release drops the extra field when it next saves. To preserve the original
deadlines through an extended rollback, retain the backup of the enriched data file and
reconcile its due fields by ticket ID before upgrading again; do not restore an old whole
file over tickets created or changed during rollback.
''')
p=Path('docs/api.md'); p.write_text(p.read_text()+'''

## Optional due times

With `DUE_TIMES=on`, ticket responses from create, get, list, patch and transition include
`due`, an ISO UTC timestamp fixed at creation. It uses the configured response hours for the
initial priority. Persisted legacy tickets receive deadlines at service startup from their
own creation timestamps and priorities. With the flag off, ticket responses keep the previous shape.

`GET /tickets?overdue=true` returns the usual `{items, next}` page containing only `open`
and `in_progress` tickets with `due` strictly earlier than now. This restriction also applies
when status or priority filters are present; their existing matching rules remain in effect.
`overdue=false` adds no restriction. Other overdue values return the normal 400 error envelope
when enabled. With the flag off the parameter is ignored as before.
''')
Path('docs/decisions/0009-fixed-due-times.md').write_text('''# 9. Fixed due times with an additive rollout

Status: Accepted

## Context

Response promises must survive priority changes, configuration changes and restarts. Operators
must be able to deploy with no API changes and roll back to 1.4.0 on the enriched data file.

## Decision

Keep data-file version 1 and add an optional validated `due` ticket field. The existing 1.4.0
reader explicitly selects known fields and ignores this addition. The store sets new deadlines
on creation and backfills missing legacy deadlines before the server listens, saving atomically.
It does not recalculate stored deadlines. This metadata expansion changes neither audit nor outbox.

`DUE_TIMES=on` controls presentation and overdue query behavior independently from storage.
Per-priority environment settings supply hours. Overdue means an active ticket strictly past
its deadline. Existing pagination and status/priority matching behavior remain intact.

## Consequences

A release can enrich production files while preserving API responses, then enable the feature
on a later restart. A migration save failure stops startup. Rollback can read every ticket,
but a 1.4.0 save discards unknown due fields; operators retain enriched backups for subsequent
reconciliation. Raw CLI output appends due after existing columns when enabled.
''')
p=Path('docs/decisions/README.md'); p.write_text(p.read_text()+'| 9 | [Fixed due times with an additive rollout](0009-fixed-due-times.md) | Accepted |\n')
p=Path('CHANGELOG.md'); p.write_text(p.read_text().replace('\n', '\n\n## 1.5.0\n\n- Persist fixed ticket due times with configurable response hours and startup backfill.\n- Expose due times and paginated overdue listings with `DUE_TIMES=on`.\n- Keep version-1 files readable by 1.4.0 and preserve existing raw CLI columns.\n',1))
Path('test-results.txt').unlink()
